title: The evaporating salt pan
prompt: A pan contains 300 g of a 12% salt solution by mass. Water evaporates, leaving 100 g total in the pan at a temperature where at most 36 g of salt dissolve per 100 g of liquid water. Find the masses of dissolved and crystalline salt. Check conservation and distinguish concentration in the liquid from salt fraction of the whole pan.

answer:
Initial salt:  
\[
0.12(300)=36\text{ g salt}
\]
Initial water:
\[
300-36=264\text{ g water}
\]

Let the final liquid water be \(w\), dissolved salt be \(d\), and crystalline salt be \(c\).

Salt conservation:
\[
d+c=36
\]
Final total mass:
\[
w+d+c=100
\]
so
\[
w+36=100 \implies w=64\text{ g liquid water}
\]

At the given temperature, the liquid water can dissolve at most
\[
36\text{ g salt per }100\text{ g water}
\]
so with \(64\text{ g}\) water, the maximum dissolved salt is
\[
d=\frac{36}{100}(64)=23.04\text{ g}
\]
Thus the crystalline salt is
\[
c=36-23.04=12.96\text{ g}
\]

So the final pan contains:
\[
\boxed{23.04\text{ g dissolved salt}}
\]
\[
\boxed{12.96\text{ g crystalline salt}}
\]

Check:
- Liquid water: \(64\text{ g}\)
- Dissolved salt: \(23.04\text{ g}\)
- Crystalline salt: \(12.96\text{ g}\)
- Total mass:  
\[
64+23.04+12.96=100\text{ g}
\]
- Total salt:  
\[
23.04+12.96=36\text{ g}
\]
which matches the original salt mass.

Distinguish the concentrations:

- In the liquid brine, salt fraction by mass is
\[
\frac{23.04}{64+23.04}\approx 0.2647=26.47\%
\]
Equivalently, the liquid contains \(36\text{ g salt per }100\text{ g water}\), i.e. saturated brine is \(36/(100+36)=26.47\%\) salt by mass.

- For the whole pan including crystals:
\[
\frac{36}{100}=36\%
\]
of the total pan mass is salt, but only part is dissolved.

\[
\boxed{\text{Dissolved salt }=23.04\text{ g},\quad \text{crystalline salt }=12.96\text{ g}.}
\]

Water evaporated:
\[
264-64=200\text{ g}
\]
